evals.name: simple-local-markdown
evals.prompt: 帮我把这个 Markdown 文件发到知识星球，明天 10 点定时发布：/tmp/zsxq-eval/simple-article.md。
evals.expected_output: Skill runs Pre-flight + Content + Publish pipelines (no image pipeline, no intermediate save-as-draft step). Scheduled publish is set for tomorrow 10:00 and the button text is verified as 定时发布 before being clicked. Skill reports back with confirmation including the scheduled date.

assertions.text: The skill ran `agent-browser close --all` exactly once at the start, before any other agent-browser command.
The skill invoked scripts/prepare_content.py with the source Markdown path single-quoted, rather than constructing Markdown-paste JS inline.
The skill verified `.ProseMirror` is present in the DOM before attempting to paste content (confirming Markdown mode).
The skill pasted body content via `eval "$(cat /tmp/zsxq_paste_content.js)"`, not via `fill` or `type`.
Because the input has no images, the skill did not run any marker-deletion or image-paste commands.
The skill did NOT click `保存` or navigate to 我的文章 before scheduling. Scheduling itself is the save, so an intermediate draft-save step would be redundant and must not occur.
The skill enabled the schedule switch, set the date to tomorrow and the time to 10:00, verified the publish button text changed to 定时发布, and clicked it.
The skill never clicked `.operation-btns .post.btn` while its text was 发布.
The skill's final message to the user mentions the scheduled date (tomorrow's date) and 10:00.

evals.name: notion-url-with-images
evals.prompt: 从这篇 Notion 笔记发到知识星球：https://www.notion.so/jarod/Weekly-AI-Digest-abc123def456。里面应该有几张配图，记得都带上。
evals.expected_output: Skill calls notion-fetch on the URL, writes the extracted Markdown body to a scratch file under /tmp/zsxq-notion/, runs notion_ingest.py to download all remote images locally, then continues with prepare_content.py on /tmp/zsxq-notion/article.md. Image positions in the final Zsxq post match their positions in the Notion source. Scheduled for tomorrow 10:00.

assertions.text: The skill called the notion-fetch MCP tool with the user-provided Notion URL before doing any browser work.
The skill ran scripts/notion_ingest.py with the Notion-fetched Markdown and an output directory under /tmp/.
Each image referenced in the Notion page exists as a local file in the notion_ingest output directory after the ingest step.
The image order in the final Zsxq post matches the image order in the Notion source exactly (first image in Notion = first image in Zsxq post, etc.).
The skill ran scripts/prepare_content.py on the article.md produced by notion_ingest.py (not on the raw Notion response).
The three-command image-insertion sequence (marker delete / wait 500 / paste) ran once per image, in order.
For each image the marker-deletion eval, the `agent-browser wait 500`, and the paste-image eval were three separate commands — not combined into a single eval.
The skill did NOT click `保存` before scheduling. Only the scheduled-publish flow was used.
The skill enabled the schedule switch, set tomorrow 10:00, verified the button text is 定时发布, and clicked it.

evals.name: notion-url-with-expired-signed-images
evals.prompt: 把这篇 Notion 文章发到星球：https://www.notion.so/jarod/Long-Article-xyz789。（测试场景：其中一张图片的 Notion signed URL 已过期，会下载失败。）
evals.expected_output: notion_ingest.py reports failed_count > 0 in its JSON summary. The skill stops, surfaces the failure to the user, and asks whether to re-fetch the Notion page (to get fresh signed URLs) or proceed with the missing image skipped. Does not silently publish a post with broken image references.

assertions.text: The skill inspected the JSON summary from notion_ingest.py and noticed failed_count > 0 rather than proceeding blindly.

On detecting failed downloads, the skill surfaced the issue to the user and asked whether to re-fetch the Notion page or to skip the missing image(s) — rather than silently publishing a post with broken references.
The skill did not click the publish button while recovering from the image failure. Whatever path is taken, scheduled publish remains the only submit.
